title: The Paul Whiteman Hour and Glen Osser
summary: Whiteman veterans and arranger Osser; Schillinger-style arrangers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, at that time, also, I went in and did the Paul Whiteman Hour, and we had half of Paul Whiteman's original band in there, for that matter, Pingatore and Joe Tardoe, Curt Deiderly on the violin. And we had Abe -- the arranger
and conductor for Paul Whiteman. (Len Osser, Abe something.
It was a different name then. Abe something else. Then he became Glen Osser.

Yeah, very competent, very quick. He could sit down and dash things off. A lot of the arrangers in those days studied from Shillinger, who had the mathematics system, because they had to grind these arrangements out. So they'd write out a formula and it would be rhythms. But mostly they would sound like that, too. The sounds would come out pretty bad.
